prize_parts.citation: for formalizing the political economy of trade policy, showing how lobbying and special-interest politics shape trade protection

statement.case_for: My preferred part is unchanged: a single-part prize on B001 for Helpman and Grossman. The protection-for-sale framework turned trade protection from an exogenous policy variable into the equilibrium of lobbying and government objectives. It generated sharp, falsifiable cross-sector predictions and a three-decade body of theory, empirical work and policy analysis. Attribution is a tightly coupled two-person partnership with central joint papers and a joint book, so no one has to be arbitrarily cut. In my own field I value theory that is built to be confronted with real data, and this framework made a qualitative idea measurable. That the testing has been mixed is part of its record, not a reason to discount it. What did change after round 1 is the citation. I now confine it to the political economy of trade policy, which is the ballot's stated discovery. I drop the clause on innovation and growth that I used in round 1. Several colleagues (Enflo, Fredriksson, Krusell, Boppart) argue that the growth strand goes beyond the ballot and may overlap with the 2025 prize. That overlap is as reported in the files and I have not verified it. A narrower citation is easier to defend and does not depend on any claim about other prizes. The growth work remains background, not the basis of the award. I weigh this on attribution, durability and maturity, not on the number of members who prefer it.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is empirical. Tests of the protection-for-sale equilibrium are mixed and sensitive to specification, so the contribution is an organising framework and research programme, not a set of confirmed parameters. A citation must not imply otherwise. A second concern is whether the committee sees this as distinct enough from the 2008 trade prize, which is a point raised in the files. A third is that Helpman is also credited on B030, so the committee must decide whether it is rewarding political economy or firm heterogeneity as the trade contribution. Finally, a narrower citation gives up part of the pair's broader legacy. If the committee wants a prize resting on densely tested findings, B002 or B018 may look stronger on the empirical record.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B002 first and now calls B001 a close alternative. He finds the mixed empirical record of protection-for-sale more worrying than the B001 supporters do. He says BLP has been validated by three decades of use, and he would not widen the B001 citation to endogenous growth.
responses.response: I agree with him on the citation and have narrowed mine accordingly. I also accept that B002's record of use in merger review and antitrust is stronger evidence of durability than anything on B001. We differ on what a prize should weigh. Protection-for-sale made a question about the political determination of policy precise and testable, and the contested tests are the evidence of that. BLP's attribution has a real cost: the three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan and Reiss and separates Pakes's dynamic-games work from the demand framework. The B001 credit needs no such cut. I keep B002 as my first alternative. If the committee decides that a methods contribution with proven policy use outweighs a framework with a mixed empirical record, I would move to it, and I do not regard that choice as unreasonable.

responses.point: Dreber ranks B030 first. She argues that firm heterogeneity and selection have been confronted more densely with micro data than protection-for-sale. She treats the mixed B001 record as a reason to prefer the firm-heterogeneity line, and she names the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as the main weakness.
responses.response: Her empirical argument has force, and I would not call B030 weaker on scientific importance. The question for a prize is whether credit can be assigned cleanly. The exporter facts and closely related models came independently from Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum. A three-name cap cannot honour them without weakening the Melitz-Helpman core, and she says herself that she cannot resolve this. I treat the two ballots as distinct achievements by Helpman. A Grossman-Helpman award does not preclude later recognition of the firm-level strand, and I would not combine the two parts. That would produce a three-person configuration and blur both citations. If the committee finds a defensible attribution for B030, I would reconsider its standing. As the files stand, B001 is better attributed.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B018 first. In round 1 she changed her proposal from Katz to Dorn and now words the citation around technology and trade shocks to labour demand. She argues that a decade of replication and re-estimation shows maturity, and that Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the cleanest attribution for the China-shock papers.
responses.response: Her revision answers the main attribution objection I raised in round 1, namely that the three-name set was unstable. Autor, Dorn and Hanson is a defensible core for a citation confined to the trade-shock evidence, and the design-based quality of that work is not in doubt. I have therefore replaced B014 with B018 as my second alternative. Two things still keep it below B001 for me. First, the task-framework antecedents (Levy and Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo) fall outside the credited names, so the citation would have to stay on the empirical evidence and not claim the framework. Second, I read the ongoing shift-share and persistence debate differently from her. It is productive, but I would want more consolidation of the long-run magnitudes before a prize rests on them. This is a weighting difference. I could support B018 in a later year, and a settled set would move me.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B001 first. She warns that the citation must be drawn carefully between trade policy and innovation-driven growth, and that the empirical weakness is the strongest reservation against her own choice. She wants the citation to say that the contribution is the theory and the research programme it created, not a settled parameter.
responses.response: I agree and have adopted that framing. The citation I now propose says the contribution is the formalization of the political economy of protection, and it makes no claim of empirical confirmation. This is a change from round 1, where I named innovation and growth. Her point on overlap with the 2025 prize is as reported and I have not verified it, but the narrower wording does not depend on it. I also share her view that swapping to the firm-heterogeneity line only to avoid the empirical issue would not help, because that line has its own attribution gap.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives to the mixed, specification-sensitive empirical record of protection-for-sale relative to its influence on theory and policy analysis. This is the main open dispute, and I could be wrong about where the committee draws the line.

Whether the narrowed citation sufficiently distinguishes the contribution from Krugman's 2008 prize. The overlap claims about 2008 and 2025 come from colleagues' files and I have not independently verified them.
Whether the committee will settle the Helpman question between B001 and B030, and whether a resolution of the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum gap would change the comparison.

Whether B002 or B018 would better survive scrutiny once the credited sets are fixed (a BLP triple that leaves out Bresnahan and Reiss; Autor, Dorn and Hanson with task-framework antecedents uncredited).
My assessments rest on general knowledge and colleagues' written statements, without independent verification of citation or impact data.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. None apparent from the supplied profile for B001 (Helpman, Grossman) or for the alternatives B002 and B018. My research is in corporate finance (venture capital, private equity, bankruptcy and carbon pricing), and my listed co-authors (Kaplan, Axelson, Weisbach, Jenkinson, Lerner, Sørensen, Robinson, Martinsson, Thomann) are not credited names on those ballots. For disclosure only: I am an adjunct professor at Chicago Booth, I have long overlapped with several committee colleagues, and I am Vice President of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. I do not treat any of these as a candidate-specific conflict. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
